newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa killer asks amnesty over U.S. student.
newsitem.headline: South Africa killer asks amnesty over U.S. student.

text.p: One of four men jailed for the murder of American student Amy Biehl has applied for amnesty from South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission headed by Archbishop Desmond Tutu.
A commission spokeswoman confirmed on Tuesday that Mongesi Manquina had applied for amnesty and said his case would be heard on May 19 in Cape Town.
Biehl, a U.S. exchange student from Orange County in California, was killed by a mob while driving just outside Cape Town on August 25, 1993. She was due to return home the next day.

The four youths who were convicted and imprisoned for 18 years were allied to the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), whose leader Clarence Makwetu later told the commission he regretted her death but his organisation would not apologise for it.
The commission has been set up to try and heal the wounds of the country's apartheid past.
